Columns that identify groups in a tidy output, as tidypopgen names them

Source: R/group_columns.R
group_columns.Rd

This function is designed for developers of packages that add methods to the generics of tidypopgen for grouped data (e.g. for genotype likelihoods), so that their tidy outputs identify the groups as the methods of tidypopgen do: a single group column when there is one grouping variable, and one column per grouping variable when there are several (as dplyr::summarise()), keeping their types (e.g. a factor keeps its levels). For outputs on pairs of groups, each group of the pair has one column per grouping variable, named with a suffix (e.g. population_1 and population_2, with suffix = "_1" and "_2"), also when there is a single grouping variable.

Usage

group_columns(keys, idx, suffix = NULL, other_names = character())

Arguments

keys

a data frame with one row per group and one column per grouping variable, as returned by dplyr::group_keys().

idx

the index of the group of each row of the output.

suffix

NULL for outputs with a row per group, or a suffix added to the names of the grouping variables, for the columns of one group of a pair.

other_names

the names of the other columns of the output: the group columns must not have any of these names (an error asks to rename the grouping variables).

Value

a tibble with one row per element of idx.

See also

group_labels() for the labels of the groups.

Examples

keys <- data.frame(population = c("a", "a", "b"), sex = c("F", "M", "F"))
group_columns(keys, c(1, 3))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   population sex  
#>   <chr>      <chr>
#> 1 a          F    
#> 2 b          F    
group_columns(keys[1], c(1, 3))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   group
#>   <chr>
#> 1 a    
#> 2 b    
group_columns(keys, c(1, 3), suffix = "_1")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   population_1 sex_1
#>   <chr>        <chr>
#> 1 a            F    
#> 2 b            F
